Devious

/DEE-vee-uhs/ - the stress falls on DEE · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Devious means not straightforward; dishonest in an indirect, scheming way.

Rather than ask for the last slice outright, my devious roommate kept inventing urgent chores until the kitchen stood empty.

Worked Example

Selling the old hatchback, Mr. Boyd was devious without telling a single outright lie: he parked it with the dented side against the hedge, booked every viewing at dusk, and steered each test drive away from the highway, where the engine's rattle would have introduced itself.

Devious fits better than 'dishonest' because it names the shape of the dishonesty: nothing false is stated, but every arrangement bends the buyer's attention away from the truth.

How Devious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

crafty

crafty: clever at getting what one wants, sometimes with grudging admiration

underhanded

underhanded: dishonest and sneaky, stressing the unfairness

scheming

scheming: constantly making secret plans that serve oneself

Antonyms

straightforward

straightforward: direct and honest, with nothing hidden

honest

honest: truthful in word and deed

How Strong Is It? — roundabout → devious → treacherous

roundabout vs. devious

roundabout vs. devious: A roundabout answer merely wanders instead of going straight; devious adds intent—the indirectness is designed to mislead.

treacherous vs. devious

treacherous vs. devious: Treacherous outdoes devious: a devious rival bends the truth to beat you, while a treacherous one betrays your trust outright and may do real harm.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of devious.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: off, away from

Root — vi

Root — vi: road, way (from Latin via)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: characterized by

Put it together

Put it together: De- (off) + vi (road) + -ous (characterized by) = off the road. Latin devius described paths that left the main highway, and English first used devious for winding back lanes. The moral sense grew straight out of the picture: a devious person leaves the plain road of honest dealing and arrives by hidden byways instead.

Use the root in a new word: viaduct

Use the root in a new word: viaduct: The old viaduct carries the road across the valley on a row of stone arches.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, mildly disapproving

Devious points at a schemer's methods: indirect, clever, bent on misleading. It differs from insidious, another word in this unit, which describes harm that creeps in while looking harmless—a plan can be devious the moment it is hatched, but we usually call something insidious only once we see the slow damage. For simple rule-breaking, plain cheating or dishonest says it better.
